title: Start here: a program prints hello
question: A program prints "hello": write(1, "hello\n", 6). kSEE recorded what the kernel did for it. Follow the three stops.

stops.note: This is the kernel's code for write(), as it ran: the lines in green ran. The timeline above shows the calls it made.
On the right, the Stack: the calls that led here, with their arguments. count is 6, the bytes of "hello\n".
Here the bytes go to the console (bottom left). Now step with ◀ ▶, a line at a time, forwards or back.
